name: Roštilj (Balkan Mixed Grill)
reasons: Technique pan_fry -> grilled; follow the stored preparation steps, not the dish title.
Include the mandatory 60 min cevapi rest.

steps.display_text: Make ćevapi: mix beef and pork mince with garlic, baking soda, salt, and pepper. Form into fingers. Rest 1 hour.
Cube chicken thighs. Marinate in oil, paprika, garlic, salt, and pepper.
Thread chicken onto skewers.
Grill everything on a very hot charcoal or gas grill, turning occasionally until cooked through with char marks.
Serve on a large platter with warm flatbread, ajvar, raw diced onion, and sour cream.

name: Salmon in Cream Sauce
reasons: Technique grilled -> pan_fry; follow the stored preparation steps, not the dish title.

steps.display_text: Season salmon with salt. Sear skin-side down in butter for 4 minutes until skin is crispy. Flip, cook 2 more minutes. Remove.
In the same pan, sauté minced shallot and garlic until soft.
Add white wine and reduce by half.
Add cream and simmer until slightly thickened. Add spinach and let it wilt.
Return salmon to the sauce. Heat through for 1–2 minutes. Finish with fresh dill and serve.

name: Samosa
reasons: Remove the under-30 tag because corrected elapsed time exceeds 30 minutes.

steps.display_text: Make pastry: rub oil into flour until crumbly. Add just enough cold water to form a stiff dough. Rest 20 minutes.
Boil potatoes, mash roughly. Fry cumin seeds in oil, add ginger and chili, then potatoes, peas, and spices. Cool.
Divide dough into balls. Roll each into a thin oval. Cut in half.
Form each half into a cone, fill with potato mixture, and seal the open edge tightly with water.
Deep-fry at 170°C for 5–6 minutes until golden and crispy. Serve with mint chutney and tamarind sauce.

name: Samsa (Central Asian Pastry)
reasons: Technique fried -> baked; follow the stored preparation steps, not the dish title.
Remove the under-30 tag because corrected elapsed time exceeds 30 minutes.

steps.display_text: Make filling: mix raw lamb mince with very finely diced raw onion, cumin, salt, and pepper.
Roll dough into circles or squares. Place filling in the centre.
Fold into a triangle and seal edges tightly.
Brush with egg wash and sprinkle with black and white sesame seeds.
Bake in a very hot oven (220°C) for 25–30 minutes until golden brown.

name: Sarma (Balkan Stuffed Cabbage)
reasons: Technique baked -> simmered; follow the stored preparation steps, not the dish title.

steps.display_text: Mix pork and beef mince with raw rice, sautéed onion, paprika, salt, and pepper.
Separate sauerkraut leaves. Place a tablespoon of filling on each leaf and roll tightly.
Layer smoked ribs on the bottom of a large pot. Pack rolls tightly on top.
Add a few whole peppercorns, bay leaves, and just enough water to cover.
Bring to a boil, then reduce to lowest heat. Cover and cook for 2–2.5 hours.
Sarma is always better the next day. Serve with sour cream and mashed potatoes.

name: Sauerbraten
reasons: Technique pan_fry -> braised; follow the stored preparation steps, not the dish title.
Minimum 3 days marinating = 4320 min, plus up to 180 min braise, 10 min browning, 30 min preparation. The longer 5-day option is excluded.

steps.display_text: Make marinade: boil vinegar, wine, onion, bay leaf, juniper berries, and cloves. Cool completely.
Submerge beef in marinade in the fridge for 3–5 days, turning daily.
Remove beef and pat dry. Strain and reserve marinade.
Brown beef on all sides in a heavy pot. Add strained marinade.
Braise covered at 160°C for 2.5–3 hours until very tender.
Crumble ginger snap cookies into the braising liquid — they thicken the sauce and add sweetness. Serve sliced with red cabbage.

name: Seared Scallops
reasons: Technique grilled -> pan_fry; follow the stored preparation steps. Cold assembled dishes use the existing raw category, which does not imply all ingredients are uncooked.

steps.display_text: Pat scallops completely dry with paper towels — this is essential for a good sear.
Season with salt and pepper just before cooking.
Heat a pan over very high heat until nearly smoking. Add a mix of oil and butter.
Place scallops in the pan without moving. Sear for exactly 90 seconds until a deep golden crust forms.
Flip once. Add garlic and thyme. Baste with butter for 60 seconds. Squeeze lemon over and serve immediately.

name: Shakshuka
reasons: Technique baked -> simmered; follow the stored preparation steps, not the dish title.

steps.display_text: Sauté diced onion and pepper in olive oil over medium heat until soft.
Add garlic, cumin, paprika, and chili. Fry for 1 minute.
Add canned tomatoes, break them up, and season with salt. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Make small wells in the sauce. Crack an egg into each well.
Cover and cook on low heat for 5–7 minutes until whites are set but yolks still runny.
Crumble feta on top, scatter fresh herbs. Serve straight from the pan with crusty bread.

name: Shashlik (Skewer BBQ)
reasons: Technique pan_fry -> grilled; follow the stored preparation steps, not the dish title.

steps.display_text: Cut pork neck into 4 cm cubes. Grate onion and combine with vinegar, oil, bay leaf, salt, and spices.
Marinate pork in the mixture for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
Thread onto metal skewers alternating with raw onion slices.
Grill over hot charcoal (not open flame) for 15–20 minutes, turning every 3–4 minutes.
Meat should be slightly charred outside and juicy inside. Serve with lavash and fresh vegetables.

name: Shawarma
reasons: Technique raw -> grilled; follow the stored preparation steps, not the dish title.
Remove the under-30 tag because corrected elapsed time exceeds 30 minutes.

steps.display_text: Marinate chicken in shawarma spices, lemon juice, and oil for at least 1 hour.
Grill or pan-fry chicken until slightly charred and cooked through. Rest 5 minutes, then slice thin.
Make toum (garlic sauce): blend garlic with lemon juice, slowly stream in oil to make a fluffy emulsion.
Warm flatbread on a hot griddle.
Spread garlic sauce on flatbread. Add chicken, tomato, onion, pickles, and a pinch of sumac.
Roll tightly in parchment and serve immediately.
